note: The no-op test with a control (COMPONENTS.md §7, decision 0019). Each scenario names one rule of the engine — every line that states it, in every file that does — a prompt that exercises it, and a check the rule is supposed to make true. The run makes two arms, one with the rule and one with every one of its homes removed, and the scenario passes only when the with-arm meets the check and the control does not. The control is expected to fail: without that delta, “the behavior differed” is the reader’s judgement rather than a result. Run 1 (2026-09-03) scored 0 of 6 because a scenario named one line and the plugin ships its own specification beside it, so the rule survived in docs/ (decision 0073). A home the rule shares with other rules carries a replaceWith — the same line with the rule’s clause taken out — so the control loses the rule and nothing else. DECISIONS.md is not swept: it is a record of how the engine came to say what it says, not an instruction, and a sweep of it would delete the reasoning a reader needs.
thresholdNote: Set in Stage 11a from run 2 (decision 0073), citing the run it came from. Run 1 could set none: its control kept the rule, because a scenario named one line and the plugin ships its own specification beside it. Until a threshold is written here, --observations reports the rate and gates nothing.

lines.line: **The pickup** (`skills/run/SKILL.md`): a slug with no task directory but a handoff file is an offer, never an automatic restore. On the developer's yes, `run` writes `plan.md` from `## Plan`, records `Init:` and `Plan: approved --tasks <n> --branch <name>` — from the default branch, so `base` is the fork point rather than the branch tip — checks the branch out, and deletes the handoff file, which is part of the same commit the developer makes next. On no, it prints the file's path and stops.
